run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:56:42Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is caused by HTTP 504 gateway timeouts, not by any failure inside frontend-proxy or frontend. Every sampled frontend-proxy error span is span_name "ingress" with http.status_code 504 and duration ~15.000s (the proxy's upstream timeout), and the slow upstream leg is the frontend's POST /api/checkout, which completes in ~15.72s while the proxy gives up at 15.0s. Inside that trace, all hops are milliseconds except checkout's span_name "orders publish" (Kafka produce to topic orders), which takes 15.58s. This is a latency regression on the Kafka produce path that began with the Kafka Deployment rollout at 04:54:11-04:54:13 (new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 deleted), which took Kafka out of service until 04:55:56 (checkout logged 'connect: connection refused' and 'circuit breaker is open' 04:54:32-04:55:43) and left the new broker with an empty log (orders-0 at offset 0, high watermark 0). The alert fired one minute after the broker returned, because from then on checkout's publishes still take 8.8-29.5s (baseline before the rollout: all orders publish spans <=2ms), so checkout requests exceed the proxy's 15s timeout. Kafka CPU/memory saturation, frontend failure and the fraud-detection OOM restart at 04:47:16 were each checked and are not supported as causes. The broker-side mechanism that keeps acknowledgements at 10-30s after the restart is not observable with the available telemetry.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error signal: its ERROR span rate is 0.0889/s at 04:56:42 (alert start) and 0.2130/s at 05:09:42 (end of window), so the alerting condition is still met at the end of the window.

All frontend-proxy error spans are on span_name "ingress"; the 10-minute ERROR increase climbs from ~2.1 at 04:46:42 to 28.4 at 04:56:42 (exactly the alert start) and to 161.7 at 05:09:42, while span_name "router frontend egress" shows 0 errors.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans carry error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with duration ~15.000-15.001s, and their parent is a load-generator POST span with error=true and http.status_code=504 (e.g. trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20).

In trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20, frontend's server span "POST" lasts 15.000791s and ends exactly at the proxy's 15s timeout, while its child route span "POST /api/checkout" completes 15.718693s with http.status_code 200; checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder lasts 15.715883s and its child span_name "orders publish" lasts 15.581950s, i.e. the whole added latency sits in the Kafka publish step.

checkout's only ERROR status spans are on span_name "orders publish": its 10-minute ERROR increase is 19.2 at 04:56:42, 14.6-15.4 through 05:05:42, and the instant ERROR rate at 05:09:42 is 0 (writes succeed again, but slowly).

Comparable baseline for the regression: for checkout span_name "orders publish" every span was in the <=2ms bucket at 04:51:42 (cumulative counts identical from le=2 to le=5000), whereas at 05:06:42 only 12.5 of 294 spans were <=10s, 116.8 were <=15s and ~177 were above 15s.

checkout's own logs show Kafka unavailability from 04:54:32: repeated exact errors "Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused", "client/metadata got error from broker -1 while fetching metadata", "Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open"; connectivity returns at 04:55:56 ("Connected to broker at kafka:9092", "producer/leader/orders/0 selected broker 1").

After reconnecting, checkout logs successful-but-slow publishes: "Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 21.972942534s" at 05:00:41 through "duration: 11.452121497s" at 05:03:52, with durations between 8.79s and 29.48s across the sampled lines.

Kubernetes events show a controller-driven kafka rollout: pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 created at 04:54:11 (SuccessfulCreate, ScalingReplicaSet kafka 0->1 of ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485) and the previous pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 stopped and deleted at 04:54:13 (Killing, SuccessfulDelete, old ReplicaSet scaled 1->0).

The new kafka pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 was created at 04:54:11, is Running/Ready with 0 container restarts, and its broker log begins at 04:55:48 with an empty log: "Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0 ... high watermark 0 ... Previous leader None", followed by consumer-group (re)formation for groups fraud-detection (04:55:53) and accounting (04:55:55).

The kafka Deployment's container limits are cpu 400m and memory 900Mi (requests 100m/300Mi); observed kafka usage peaked at 0.2997 cores and 7.41 throttled CFS periods/s at 04:55:42 (startup) but fell to ~0.02 cores and 0.03-0.16 throttled periods/s from 04:57 on, and working set stayed flat at ~615-627MB of the 900Mi limit.

Between 05:02:37 and 05:03:40 the new kafka broker continuously wrote KRaft metadata snapshots (e.g. "Creating new KRaft snapshot file ... because we have replayed at least 2800 bytes" every ~15s and deletion of older segments/snapshots by 60000ms retention), showing ongoing internal metadata churn while client writes were taking 10-30s.

frontend is not failing: its ERROR span increase is 0 at every step of the window, and in the traced checkout request its own downstream gRPC calls (ProductCatalogService/GetProduct) take ~1.5-1.6ms; the frontend is merely blocked on checkout.

checkout's other downstream dependencies are not the slow hop: in the same error traces, checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans are ~1.5ms, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert ~1.5-1.6ms, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct ~1.5-1.6ms and cart EmptyCart ~1.6ms.

Other namespace services showed no tied error signal: 10-minute ERROR-span increases are 0 throughout for accounting, fraud-detection, frontend and payment, while ad (~1.05 per 10m from 04:36) and recommendation (~1.05 per 10m from 04:11) carry small steady error counts that already existed before the alert and are not linked to the 504 burst.

Rejected: the fraud-detection restart caused the alert. Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm shows lastState terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled finished at 04:47:16 with 2 restarts (BackOff event 04:47:17, container Started again 04:47:30), i.e. 7 minutes before the kafka rollout, and its own ERROR-span increase is 0, so nothing ties it to the 504s.

Rejected: resource saturation of the kafka container explains the remaining 10-30s publish latency. After the 04:55 startup burst the container used only ~0.02 cores of its 400m limit with low throttling, and its working set stayed ~620MB against a 900Mi limit with 0 restarts, so CPU/memory exhaustion is not supported.

The alert is explained by this chain: the kafka Deployment rollout at 04:54:11-04:54:13 removed the only broker, checkout could not produce to topic orders until 04:55:56, and after the broker returned checkout's produce to orders still waited 8.8-29.5s (vs <=2ms before the rollout), so POST /api/checkout took ~15.7s, exceeding frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, and the proxy returned 504 on span_name "ingress".

The remaining 10-30s publish latency most likely originates inside the newly started broker (fresh empty log directory: orders-0 at offset 0/high watermark 0, continuous KRaft metadata snapshot churn at 05:02-05:03) rather than in checkout or its callers; this is unverified because broker-side latency, disk and request-queue state are not instrumented.

Verify from change history why the kafka Deployment was rolled out at 04:54:11 and whether the previous revision is recoverable; the new pod's kafka log directory came up empty (orders-0 at offset 0), so the rollout also discarded topic data, which matters for consumers accounting and fraud-detection.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data, so the exact expression and the reported 0.4 value could not be reproduced (the measured frontend-proxy ERROR span rate is 0.089/s at 04:56:42 and 0.213/s at 05:09:42).

Kafka is not instrumented as a traced service: traces_list_operations for service "kafka" returned no_data, and no Kafka broker/JMX metrics exist in this Prometheus, so broker request latency, disk I/O, ISR and throttle state inside the new broker are unknown and the 10-30s acknowledgement delay cannot be attributed to a specific broker mechanism.
fetch_pod_logs for checkout-5dccddf8bb-6qppz returned no lines between 05:04:30 and 05:09:43 (lines_read 0), so produce durations after 05:03:52 are unknown from logs.

Whether the kafka rollout changed the image or only configuration could not be verified: the previous pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 no longer exists and secrets/change history are not readable in this Run (change_history integration is not integrated).

frontend-proxy span metrics carry no route label, so it is not proven that only POST checkout requests get 504s: every sampled error span was on the checkout POST flow, but other load-generator journeys (user_browse_product, user_add_to_cart, user_view_cart, user_get_ads, user_get_recommendations, user_index, user_checkout_multi) have no span-metric series and were not individually verified.

No ERROR series were returned for cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, email or image-provider in this window; their error state is unknown rather than proven zero, although the sampled traces show those calls completing in milliseconds.
next_steps: Look up the change/rollout that replaced kafka ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 with kafka-5c9d7cc485 at 04:54:11 and confirm whether it was intended; compare the previous and current Deployment spec and image digest.

Inspect the new broker directly for request-queue time, disk/flush latency of the /tmp/kafka-logs emptyDir volume, KRaft metadata churn and ISR health, since client-measured produce latency stayed at 8-30s while container CPU was ~0.02 cores.

Confirm whether produce latency and the frontend-proxy 504 rate recover on their own, and while they do not, consider whether the frontend-proxy upstream timeout or the checkout Kafka publish path needs to be addressed (e.g. give kafka sufficient CPU/durable storage and avoid rolling a single-broker Kafka under load).
Read the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule file for RequestErrorRate to confirm the expression and threshold that produced the reported 0.4 value.
